figure: Figure 3.4 — Dense vs MoE parameter allocation and KV cache behavior
issue: The red KV comparison callout is duplicated verbatim under both the Dense 70B and MoE columns: both read “dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB.” Because each callout sits inside a single model column, the layout implies that both columns contain the same two-value comparison rather than assigning 12 GB to the dense model and 0.6 GB to the MoE model. This is especially risky because the figure’s central claim is that the KV difference comes from attention shape, not MoE routing; the duplicated callout visually reinforces the opposite reading.
evidence: Rendered page shows two separate red boxes, one under the Dense 70B column and one under the MoE column, both containing the identical text “dense 12 GB vs MoE 0.6 GB.” The caption correctly states “~12 GB vs ~0.6 GB at 9.2K/8-bit” and “the gap is the shape, not the routing,” but the figure itself does not visually assign the values to the correct columns.
acceptance_test: Replace the two duplicated red callouts with either (a) one shared comparison callout spanning both columns, or (b) column-specific labels: “Dense KV ≈ 12 GB” under Dense 70B and “MoE KV ≈ 0.6 GB” under MoE, with a shared note that the difference is due to attention shape, not routing. Re-render and verify that a reader cannot infer that both models have both KV values.
